title: Deuxième partie : variations sur l'équation des lacets [suite à La "Longue Marche" à travers la théorie de Galois…, pages 293 à 650, dont table des matières] : notes et copies de notes manuscrites (s.d.).

deep.reconstruction:
Context: in the 'Deuxième partie' of the Longue Marche notes, Grothendieck studies the scheme of solutions (ξ, η, μ) of a system of matrix equations, (33)–(35), in a rank-2 module M over a base. This is a linearized, 2-dimensional version of his 'loop equation' (équation des lacets), apparently aimed at describing 2-dimensional (SL2-type) representations compatible with the elliptic generators ρ (order 6) and σ (order 4) of SL2(Z). On the previous page he showed that this solution scheme is smooth of relative dimension 2. There he used P(ξ) = Tr ξ(λ0ρ + σ) and took ρ = [[0,1],[-1,1]] and σ = [[0,-1],[1,0]]. A check shows that P(ξ) = D forces λ0 = 1, and then λ0ρ + σ = E22.

The unipotent one-parameter group is ε1(λ) = [[1,0],[λ,1]], so that η ε1(μ-1) = [[R+(μ-1)S, S],[T+(μ-1)U, U]], as in (51).

On this page:
(1) The equation ξ = η ε1(μ-1) implies B = S and D = U, by comparing the second columns.
(2) Grothendieck asserts that, given the determinant and trace conditions (54) on ξ and η, the equation is equivalent to one of these two equalities together with μD = 1 (equivalently μU = 1). The conditions (54) are det ξ = det η = 1 plus one linear trace condition on each matrix. For η the condition T − S = 1 is Tr(ησ) = −1.
(3) Hence the solution scheme of (33)–(35) is the scheme of pairs (D, B) with D invertible, i.e. Gm × A^1. Alternatively it is the scheme of pairs (S, U) with U invertible; the manuscript says 'S'.
(4) He identifies this scheme with the affine ('ax+b') group of matrices [[μ, M],[0, 1]] = [[1/D, B/D],[0,1]], with a back-reference to p. 410. This group normalizes the one-parameter unipotent subgroup ε0(λ) = [[1,−λ],[0,1]] = ρ^{-1} ε1(λ) ρ. I verified this conjugation identity.

On the next page he returns to the general case. He introduces N0 with ε0 = 1 + N0, the normalizer B0 of L0 = {ε0(λ)}, the subgroup B̃0 where det equals the character on N0, and the exact sequence 1 → L0 → B̃0 → Gm → 1. So this page is the explicit model computation showing that the 2-dimensional smooth solution scheme is a torsor-like copy of a Borel-type group.
errors: The trace condition on ξ in (54) is transcribed as 'A+D−B = 1', but the natural one is Tr(ξρ) = C + D − B. The image is ambiguous, and the first letter could well be C.

With ε1 as in (51) and T − S = 1, one gets C + D − B = (T − S) + μU = 1 + μU. With μU = 1 this is 2, not 1. Either the trace constant for ξ, the normalization of ε1, or my reading of (54) differs, so the asserted equivalence cannot be fully checked from the page as transcribed. This is a minor bookkeeping issue in a sign or constant.
'(S,U) avec S inv.' should logically be 'U inv.', since μU = 1. This is probably a slip of the pen or a misreading.

ideas.what: Explicit computation of the solution scheme of a linearized loop equation in SL2 with elliptic elements ρ (order 6) and σ (order 4), showing it is Gm × A^1.
ideas.modern_name: Moduli/representation scheme of SL2-valued solutions; Borel subgroup (affine group) as the solution space

ideas.what: Identification of the solution scheme with the normalizer (affine group) of the unipotent subgroup ρ^{-1}ε1ρ, leading to the exact sequence 1 → L0 → B̃0 → Gm → 1 on the next page.
ideas.modern_name: Borel subgroup as normalizer of a unipotent one-parameter subgroup; extension of Gm by Ga
ideas.where_published: SGA 3 treats such group schemes in general; this specific use is unpublished

deep.surprise_reason: This is an explicit, routine matrix computation in a worked example (the SL2 case with ρ and σ). It is mathematically elementary and serves the larger unpublished 'équation des lacets' study, but the page itself contains nothing a specialist would find new.
transcription_corrections: 'équations simultanées (53) à (55)' should read '(33) à (35)', matching the previous page's reference to (33):(35).
'elle équivaut à l'une des ces deux équations et des (53)' should read '...et de (53)'.
'Là [-...-] solution' should probably read 'Le schéma des solutions des relations ... est donc celui des (D,B) avec D inv.'
'qui normalisant le sous-groupe à 1 paramètre' should read 'qui normalisent le sous-groupe à 1 paramètre'.
In the last line the struck-out symbols precede 'ε0(λ) = [[1,−λ],[0,1]] = ρ^{-1} ε1(λ) ρ'.
